source: original B00-B24 execution steps, expanded with task-specific acceptance

batches.name: Build foundation and reproducible validation
batches.goal: Implement toolchain-pinned monorepo; establish licensing/security notices; initialize Rust crates, TS packages and Go modules; create reference source applications; import the baseline capability JSON and gap register; define ADR workflow and CI paths.
batches.acceptance:
Clean clone reproducibly builds native and WASM compiler stubs plus Go/TS; no unpinned generated dependencies; fixture app runs; CI catches deliberate failure.

For each completed step record: test command, fixture set, expected behavior, actual behavior, performance measurements when relevant, dependency/IR change list, and rollback procedure. A passing demo alone does not close the batch.
batches.stop: Research gate: dev environment complexity must remain controlled; no application-specific hacks.
batches.planned_paths: repo root; compiler/; frontend/; backend/; tests/; docs/deep/

batches.name: Validate browser and language boundaries
batches.goal: Spike extension MV3/Chrome policies, CDP and Playwright capture, local bridge, TS↔Rust WASM IPC, alternate WebDriver BiDi probe. Measure real serialization and lifecycle behavior before fixing interfaces.
batches.acceptance:
Chrome MV3 policy design review; Rust native and WASM canonical results equal on sample data; subcomponent latency breakdown recorded; no secret leak.

For each completed step record: test command, fixture set, expected behavior, actual behavior, performance measurements when relevant, dependency/IR change list, and rollback procedure. A passing demo alone does not close the batch.
batches.stop: If MV3 remotely supplied plans violate policy, define a restricted data contract or move interpreter to companion; do not silently ignore.

batches.name: Define and validate versioned IR contracts
batches.goal: Finalize schema authority, typed IDs, evidence, uncertainty, authorization, effects and version axes. Create multi-language generated bindings and semantic migration fixtures.
batches.acceptance:
Two-language encode/decode round trip preserves semantics; incompatible schemas fail closed; source permission not implied by schema artifact.

For each completed step record: test command, fixture set, expected behavior, actual behavior, performance measurements when relevant, dependency/IR change list, and rollback procedure. A passing demo alone does not close the batch.
batches.stop: Do not allow large primitive implementation until this has integration signoff.

batches.name: Build primitive registry and conformance harness
batches.goal: Transform 924 candidate catalog into typed, dependency-aware requirements registry. Implement codegen/conformance harness, not 924 stubs disguised as features.
batches.acceptance:
Catalog parses, all records classified or tagged UNRESOLVED, graph has no accidental dependency cycles; tests fail if implemented claim lacks witness.

For each completed step record: test command, fixture set, expected behavior, actual behavior, performance measurements when relevant, dependency/IR change list, and rollback procedure. A passing demo alone does not close the batch.
batches.stop: Rule: test coverage rather than number of registry names.

batches.name: Implement browser observation and incremental events
batches.goal: Capture controlled DOM/AX/layout/URL/Mutation and origin-scoped observation epochs with appropriate permissions. Establish stale/missing evidence behavior.
batches.acceptance:
Fixture updates reconcile without full scan for small changes; inaccessible frame not fabricated; unsafe observation is blocked; no user content sent to cloud in local mode.

For each completed step record: test command, fixture set, expected behavior, actual behavior, performance measurements when relevant, dependency/IR change list, and rollback procedure. A passing demo alone does not close the batch.
batches.stop: Capture capability differs by runtime: advertise limits.

batches.name: Build semantic recognition and evidence engine
batches.goal: Implement indexed deterministic matching over compact ObservationIR with provenance, dependency invalidation and explicit ambiguity outcomes.
batches.acceptance:
Held-out apps with different frameworks recognize common form/grid classes with no vendor-specific conditions; no false high-confidence bindings in adversarial fixtures.

For each completed step record: test command, fixture set, expected behavior, actual behavior, performance measurements when relevant, dependency/IR change list, and rollback procedure. A passing demo alone does not close the batch.
batches.stop: If match ambiguity frequent, favor extra evidence or original surface rather than speculative selection.

batches.name: Build presentation compiler and minimal accessible renderer
batches.goal: Render semantics into accessible, customizable neutral UI with correct source-state bindings, responsive layout and preservation fallback.
batches.acceptance:
User can switch layouts without changing source effect; screen reader/keyboard conformance for fixtures; unknown editor remains usable via fallback.

For each completed step record: test command, fixture set, expected behavior, actual behavior, performance measurements when relevant, dependency/IR change list, and rollback procedure. A passing demo alone does not close the batch.
batches.stop: Do not write own terminal/3D frameworks at this stage.

batches.name: Implement verified deterministic execution
batches.goal: Operation lifecycle and effects-aware runtime; sources remain authoritative, no false success. Add source adapter/transport interfaces.
batches.acceptance:
Both direct API and browser plan complete a verified fixture; ambiguous write never automatically retries; denied caller cannot mutate source.

For each completed step record: test command, fixture set, expected behavior, actual behavior, performance measurements when relevant, dependency/IR change list, and rollback procedure. A passing demo alone does not close the batch.
batches.stop: If source effect unobservable, expose raw interaction or preservation only.

batches.name: Build version registry, semantic diff and pins
batches.goal: Make versioning a real system: multi-axis manifests, semantic diff, source compatibility, pinning, promotion and rollback independent of data rollback.
batches.acceptance:
Pin→change→diff→test→promote/degrade→rollback works; source-removed operation never pretends available; data rollback not implied.

For each completed step record: test command, fixture set, expected behavior, actual behavior, performance measurements when relevant, dependency/IR change list, and rollback procedure. A passing demo alone does not close the batch.
batches.stop: Treat versioning as product feature from day one, not optional after initial release.

batches.name: Integrate extension and secure local bridge
batches.goal: Deliver end-to-end extension interaction with original source session; separate optional premium localhost bridge design.
batches.acceptance:
Install extension, transform two fixtures, perform safe operation, restore source UI; malicious web origin cannot invoke local service; extension complies with review design.

For each completed step record: test command, fixture set, expected behavior, actual behavior, performance measurements when relevant, dependency/IR change list, and rollback procedure. A passing demo alone does not close the batch.
batches.stop: Native pairing should not be confused with permission to source accounts.

batches.name: Expose API, CLI and MCP vertical slice
batches.goal: Generate interfaces from a single verified operation; no hand-implemented business logic per surface.
batches.acceptance:
One operation from same contract succeeds through all four surfaces; breaking source change degrades appropriately; no invented high-level API for unverified behavior.

For each completed step record: test command, fixture set, expected behavior, actual behavior, performance measurements when relevant, dependency/IR change list, and rollback procedure. A passing demo alone does not close the batch.
batches.stop: Do not expand endpoint counts without shared semantics and tests.

batches.name: Expand common application coverage
batches.goal: Coverage-driven expansion of forms, tables, navigation, files, calendars and ordinary enterprise workflows, based on held-out failures.
batches.acceptance:
Demonstrated workflow coverage improvement across unseen applications; regression/no silent side effects; common UI still responsive.

Users can understand why versions changed and safely roll back artifacts; paid advanced history works without restricting base safety.
